findings.title: Guard fallback-hash lookup for custom auth users
findings.suggested_fix: Treat get_session_auth_fallback_hash as optional. If absent, proceed with the existing flush-and-anonymous behavior; otherwise compare the yielded fallback hashes.
findings.why_it_matters: get_user() has historically accepted any user object exposing get_session_auth_hash(), but the new mismatch path assumes that every such object also exposes get_session_auth_fallback_hash(). For custom user objects or backends that implement the former without inheriting AbstractBaseUser, a stale or invalid session hash now raises AttributeError and returns a 500 instead of flushing the session and treating the request as anonymous.

residual_risks: With the signed-cookie session backend, an old session cookie remains independently valid while its signing secret remains in SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS. cycle_key() emits a new cookie but cannot revoke the old stateless cookie, so a retained cookie can be replayed during the configured fallback window. Remove compromised or expired fallback secrets promptly; this is the continued validity inherent in the configured grace period.

testing_gaps.title: Cover password revocation while a fallback secret is configured
testing_gaps.why_it_matters: The new test covers preserving a valid session with a matching fallback secret, while existing password-change invalidation coverage runs without SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS. The changed fallback branch must still reject the old session hash after a password change even when its signing secret remains configured; otherwise key rotation could inadvertently keep revoked sessions alive.
testing_gaps.suggested_fix: Add a test that creates a session under the old secret, changes the user's password, then calls get_user with a new SECRET_KEY and the old secret in SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS; assert it returns AnonymousUser and flushes the session.
